findings.where: Article specimen, the pull quote “Whichever PPP Law I am currently working on with a client country!” (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The pull quote is static text set in logo blue. The tile's own palette gives that blue to the wordmark, links and the button. So in an article, a large blue run of text looks like a link, and a reader may tap it and get nothing. Because this tile sets the rule for every article page, it also teaches Angélique to use the link colour for emphasis.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank reader on a phone, who taps the blue quote expecting a source or a related article and gets nothing. Also Angélique, who will copy this treatment into later posts, where blue then means two things.

findings.where: Hero, the primary action “Get in touch →” (mailto link), desktop and phone
findings.fault: The page's one action is a bare mailto link, and Mark's email address appears nowhere on the page. If the visitor has no desktop mail app set up, the click does nothing or opens an unconfigured client, and there's no address to copy. The arrow also suggests moving to a contact page rather than opening a mail program.
findings.who_objects: A staff member at a multilateral bank on a locked-down work laptop or using webmail. They decide to contact Mark, click, nothing useful happens, and they can't find the address anywhere to copy it.

findings.where: Motion sketch, “Play again” (a button), next to the article specimen's “Streamlining the PPP Process…” link
findings.fault: “Play again” replays the animation in place, but it is styled exactly like the article's underlined blue link. On this one sheet, the same look means both ‘go somewhere’ and ‘do something here’, so the tile doesn't show the next rounds a button style for a minor action.
findings.who_objects: The layout and animation rounds that build from this tile, which will have no separate look for an in-place action. A visitor who expects a link to take them somewhere will be surprised when the page stays put.
